references.text: Jericho was burned with fire as a holy ban to the Lord, in the same way as the city mentioned in Deuteronomy 13:17
Joshua curses anyone who rebuilds Jericho, reflecting the prohibition against rebuilding the banned city
Achan's sin with the devoted things shows the consequences of failing to follow the command to destroy all plunder
Ai was burned and made a permanent ruin heap, just as described in Deuteronomy 13:17
The command to burn idols and not covet silver or gold from them, parallel to burning the plunder
Laws concerning what is devoted (cherem) and how it should be treated
Saul was commanded to completely destroy Amalek and all they owned, similar to total destruction
The prophecy of Babylon's destruction, that it shall never be rebuilt, reflects the curse of an eternal ruin heap
Prophecy that cities shall become ruin heaps that are never rebuilt
Babylon shall be burned with fire as God's judgment, parallel to burning the apostate city
